author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reflected on a verse from Isaiah urging people to forget the former things and stop dwelling on the past, arguing most of us are locked in a kind of near hypnosis by culture and old habits, trapped in an identity we never really chose. He was careful to draw a line though, insisting this isn't about shutting off emotionally or going numb, some things are simply too painful to revisit. He shared how there's a specific song tied to his dog Bear's final moments that he knows he'll never be able to listen to again. Russell reframed the verse as something genuinely hopeful rather than avoidant, less about running from grief and more about trusting there's still a new path being made, even after devastating loss.

title: Time is ticking...

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reflected on how becoming a father changed something fundamental in him, realizing you can't truly be a father to anyone else until you've first become one to yourself, accepting that who you are is already enough. He pushed back against what he called the broad cultural message, that you're insufficient until you acquire the right body, possessions, approval, or affiliations, arguing it isn't personal to any one person, it's practically universal. Russell pointed out how often wildly successful people describe feeling inferior or not good enough as the very thing that drove them, and wondered aloud whether they were ever really driven at all, or simply dragged forward by insecurity and shame the whole time. Sometimes the story behind the achievement is quieter and sadder than the achievement itself.
